claim: Stem calls Lamine Yamal's €1 billion release clause "a record-setting figure". €1bn is Barcelona's standard maximum buyout clause, already carried by Ansu Fati, Pedri, Gavi and Ronald Araújo among others — Yamal matched the ceiling, he did not set a record. The keyed answer (€1 billion) is correct.
q: What is the release clause on Lamine Yamal's Barcelona contract — a record-setting figure?

claim: Stem describes Porto (2004 UCL win) as Mourinho's "first major job". Porto was his fourth managerial post: Benfica (Sept–Dec 2000), União de Leiria (2001-02), then Porto from Jan 2002. Benfica is unambiguously a major job, so the temporal/superlative clause is untrue.
q: Which manager won the Champions League with Porto in 2004 — his first major job?

claim: Stem asserts Capello won Serie A with "a record 3 different Italian clubs" including Juventus. Both of his Juventus titles (2004-05, 2005-06) were revoked in the Calciopoli ruling — 2004-05 unassigned, 2005-06 awarded to Inter — so officially he has Milan and Roma only. The 'record 3 clubs' superlative rests on titles that no longer exist in the record books.
q: Fabio Capello won Serie A with which clubs during his career — a record 3 different Italian clubs?

claim: Stem says the Bundesliga's 2017-18 VAR introduction made it "the first top league to do so". Serie A introduced VAR in the same 2017-18 season (opening weekend 19-20 Aug 2017, one day after the Bundesliga's), and Australia's A-League had already used VAR from April 2017. 'First' is at best a one-day technicality and is commonly stated as Bundesliga and Serie A jointly.
q: German football introduced the Video Assistant Referee (VAR) in which Bundesliga season — making it the first top league to do so?

claim: The stem's own wording eliminates half the option set without any football knowledge: "didn't reach the final" rules out "2nd (runners-up)", and "went unbeaten through the entire 1978 World Cup" rules out "Eliminated in group stage". A zero-knowledge player is left with a straight 3rd/4th coin flip.
q: Brazil famously went unbeaten through the entire 1978 World Cup but didn't reach the final — where did they finish?

claim: Stem says "In 2005, which Italian club was stripped of their 2004-05 Serie A title due to the 'Calciopoli' match-fixing scandal?" The scandal broke in May 2006 and the FIGC stripped Juventus of the 2004-05 title (and revoked 2005-06) in July 2006 — nothing was stripped in 2005. The keyed answer (Juventus) is right, but the stem dates the whole affair a year early.
q: In 2005, which Italian club was stripped of their 2004-05 Serie A title due to the 'Calciopoli' match-fixing scandal?
